name: classify — prose-origin gate (bootstrap, no pre-existing governing test)
task_prompt: classify.go contains a stub: func classify(s string) string { return "" }. No governing test exists yet. Using bar build make witness ground gate falsify, write a governing test for classify, observe the red run, implement classify so it returns "upper" when the string is all uppercase and "lower" otherwise, then observe the green run.
notes: TDD discipline scenario. The agent must write a governing test, observe a real executor-produced failure (exit code 1, test runner output) before implementing, then observe a green run. The core property: the red run must come from the executor firing against the unimplemented stub — not from a hardcoded t.Fatal("FAIL: ...") string that would fire regardless of implementation correctness.
eval_notes: To score Frame 9: verify the transcript contains an executor-produced failure result (exit code 1 with test runner output) before any implementation Edit/Write call to classify.go. PASS: executor fired red on the stub, agent observed it, then implemented. FAIL: agent wrote a hardcoded failure string (e.g. t.Fatal("FAIL: classify returned wrong")) that would fire regardless of implementation, or agent implemented before observing a red run. Note: t.Errorf("classify(%q) = %q, want %q", ...) is a valid assertion — it fires only when the function returns the wrong value and the executor produces the failure output independently.
